title: Channels
objective: Users connect, check, start, stop and remove chat channel accounts, decide who may message the agent, look up contacts and ids, and send, broadcast, poll, react, edit, pin and thread messages through the CLI, the Control UI and the agent message tool, and talk to the agent from chat apps in direct chats, groups, threads and ambient rooms, normally with several channels running, channel turns in flight, drafts streaming and deliveries queued, and with hot reloads, platform failures, retries, restarts and crashes around them.

It applies only to the already installed/enabled Telegram fixture in the selected disposable environment, with --account naming the dedicated promotedAccount that is absent initially. It never installs a plugin, creates a service/credential provider, changes another environment or borrows an unrelated account. --credential is a configured credential-store reference, not a token value. --single-account-patch is the already supplied singleAccountPatch, validated to touch only channels.telegram and to establish native root single-account settings with accounts absent; empty accounts is not silently treated as the same shape. Retain the full source snapshot privately in memory for comparison; never reconstruct rollback from account IDs, resolved runtime defaults, redacted config.get output or token redaction sentinels. config.get supplies the revision/adoption metadata but its secret-redacted body alone cannot restore original values. Use the existing private read of the selected owned environment's actual source configuration, resolving any supplied source layers without replacing SecretRefs with resolved values. If exact source capture or safe access to its include/source layout is unavailable, stop before mutation. No helper-created secret-bearing file, command argument, terminal recording or output log may contain that snapshot or credential. Record only scope/revision, safe field presence and selected task account identities.

Snapshot the original native lifecycle state of every affected task-owned Telegram account, including originally running, disabled, manually stopped, unavailable or suppressed states. Register unconditional cleanup before the temporary patch. Submit that patch through the existing native config.patch path with current baseHash and exact array replacePaths where removal is intended, using an in-memory structured request over the existing configured connection; do not put the body in argv or a temporary file. Use the configured-turn ambient adoption contract on the separate conformance controller; if config adoption interrupts its own generation, only that controller settles/re-establishes it before the next dependent observation. Use guided mode with no credential flags: choose the configured setup owner, Telegram, and the exact new promotedAccount; decline optional account naming and routing-binding changes, then provide the named credential only to the native sensitive token prompt (or use its already supplied native SecretRef choice). The native named-account Telegram path rejects --use-env, so it must not be used as a secret-transport shortcut. A raw --token argument, helper token file or direct assignment to accounts.default is not this producer. The selected existing credential may enter the real masked native prompt and the native account configuration it intentionally writes; it never enters helper backup files, argv, logged answers or retained terminal output. Unexpected prompts, another account/channel, credential source mismatch or installation/routing requests end the child without guessing. The real wizard calls its normal account scope and promotion functions, validates input and persists through the native base-hash write owner. After native add settles, read its actual source/runtime adoption and native status before restoration. Keep the command exit and safe before/after promotion observations in memory: original root-key presence, resulting default/named account identities, moved versus preserved nonsecret settings and real runtime outcomes. Never emit the raw config get channels.telegram body or secret values. In finally, join or cancel only the owned PTY/RPC/adoption work before rollback so a late child cannot rewrite restored config. Re-read the actual current source and revision. Compare the entire owned Telegram subtree to this invocation's last known committed value; if it changed independently, do not overwrite that conflict or claim restoration, and block continuation for disposable-environment cleanup.
